rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_supervised-claude-agentic: proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=3, proj_kernel=3, proj_sx=0.01, proj_sy=0.3, proj_sr=0.0005, img_kernel=5, img_sx=0.5, img_sy=0.5, img_sr=0.02, epochs=10, batch_size=1, lr=0.005, optimizer=adam, lambda_neg=1.0, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=400, val_n=200, val_chunk=10, seed=42, rationale=iter-2 dual_domain_bilateral_supervised, re-split Breast-CT val=200. SIX-BOX vs iter-1 (1BF/domain, hr=0.2158, ssim=0.9742, 93s). (1) PRIOR: onboarding cleared FBP baseline at hr=0.2158 but only 6 trainable params and 93s used of 20-min budget -> heavily capacity-starved; the OLD-split TPE best used img_n_bf=7 (7 chained image BFs) and reached hr=0.263. (2) Failure mode: a SINGLE image-domain bilateral has too small an effective receptive field to remove sparse-view streaks. (3) ONE KNOB: img_n_bf 1 -> 3 (3 chained image BFs = larger effective RF at +6 params; proj side/kernels/lr/epochs unchanged). (4) HYPOTHESIS: chaining 3 image BFs (Wagner 2022 cascade) enlarges the effective receptive field and lifts hr above 0.2158 toward ~0.24-0.27, because the OLD-split TPE found deep image BF stacks strongly beneficial; params ~12 still tiny. (5) BUDGET: 3x image BF forward is still cheap (BF kernels 5x5); << 20 min. (6) Loop continues; iter-3 pivots to img_n_bf deeper (->7) if this helps, else to img_kernel. Artifacts recon_raw.npz + model_ckpt.pt saved.
